C0127.title: New 'Wool-Pulling' Fraudulent Ordering Scam Drains Idle Taobao Store Deposits
C0127.summary: In October 2022, China Youth Daily reported that Mr. Liu, a Shanghai Taobao seller whose shop had been idle for nearly three years, received a burst of orders despite not operating the shop. Complaints were upheld for 27 of 29 orders, causing the platform to deduct 2,322 yuan from his deposit as compensation. Another seller, Ms. Qin, experienced a similar situation and also had deposit funds deducted. Buyers used virtual numbers to place concentrated orders and complain about non-delivery, abusing buyer-protection compensation rules for malicious arbitrage.

references.title: New 'Woolgathering' Scam via Malicious Ordering? Taobao Store Idle but Deducted Thousands in Deposits...
